title: Apries
summary: King of Egypt, son of Psammis, overthrown by Amasis (Herodotus 2.161–169); the Pharaoh-hophra of Jeremiah 44:30.
description: Added from the Herodotus import (The Histories, tr. Rawlinson). Herodotus gives reign lengths and synchronisms, not BC years, and no tier 1–4 chronology dates this person, so there is no sort year.

sorting_basis.note: No tier gives a birth year (Herodotus is display-only and gives none).

standby.note: Standby placement only. Chronological Framework of Ancient History prints this BC/AD year on the reign entry (Start: 589; End: 567). It is not a sort year. No Anno Mundi, regnal length, or Julian Period figure was converted to obtain it.

birth.note: pending CFAH reference (no CFAH anchor point or Table 1 entry found for this)

reign.citation: Griffith & White, "CFAH-9: The 19th and 26th Dynasties of Egypt," OSF preprint v1.4 (25 Sep 2025), doi:10.17605/OSF.IO/HV3B2, file CFAH-9_Dynasties_19_and_26_v1.4.pdf, Table 2 "Integrated Chronology of Dynasties 19 and 26", p. 58
reign.note: Row "Merneptah / Hophra/Apries" of Table 2 (Egypt Dynasties 19 and 26). CFAH-9 identifies Merneptah of Dynasty 19 with Hophra (Apries).

reign.date: “The length of his reign was twenty-five years”
reign.citation: Herodotus, Histories 2.161 (tr. George Rawlinson; Roman Roads Media etext, 2013), p. 167 (PDF p. 169)
reign.note: Apries attacked Sidon and fought the king of Tyre at sea. DERIVED (not Herodotus's figure): about 595/594–570/569 BC (anchor CFAH AP-8 + Amasis 44 + Psammenitus ½). Consistent: Generations dates the fall of Jerusalem to 586 BC (provisional), inside the derived reign of Pharaoh-hophra (Jer 44:30).

reign.date: “put themselves under the rule of Apries, the Egyptian monarch”
reign.citation: Herodotus, Histories 4.159 (tr. George Rawlinson; Roman Roads Media etext, 2013), p. 303 (PDF p. 305)
reign.note: Synchronism: the Libyans under Adicran appeal to Apries in the reign of Battus the Prosperous of Cyrene.

reign.date: “the subjects of Apries, who laid the blame of the defeat on him, revolted from his authority”
reign.citation: Herodotus, Histories 4.159 (tr. George Rawlinson; Roman Roads Media etext, 2013), p. 303 (PDF p. 305)
reign.note: The Egyptian defeat at Irasa leads to the revolt that made Amasis king (2.161–169). DERIVED (not Herodotus's figure): The revolt ends Apries's 25 years: about 570/569 BC on the chain from CFAH AP-8 (see 2.161).
